raw_comment:
I noticed much of the money went towards individuals and families to stimulate the economy and provide those who were unemployed with extra cash. While this money was needed to keep the economy from crashing, it certainly contributes to the problems we are seeing in 2022.

I wonder what would of happened if we didn't provide individuals and families with the majority of the money and focused more on funding healthcare? Would our economy of collapsed? Would we of been able to stop put an end to COVID faster?

While this doesn't relate to me directly, it relates to my friends and those around me. I had a friend who was a lifeguard at a pool that closed during COVID which entitled him to unemployment benefits. I watched him not work at all and make more money than he ever has before. However, as a 16-17 year old who doesn't have a strong understanding in financials, he spent it all.

This graph shows how the $5 trillion of pandemic stimulus funding was distributed. We can see that individuals and families were at the top of the list and healthcare was the smallest area that had a dedicated section, even though you can argue health care funding would of been the most important. The graph also indirectly shows the government's priorities and the political agenda of those with power.

A catchy headline for this graph would be "Did Money Solve, or Create a Problem?"

raw_comment:
I noticed that much of the stimulus spending went towards keeping the economy alive and running rather than healthcare aid. This was especially true during the early and middle parts of the pandemic, when businesses were closing down and job layoffs skyrocketed.

I wonder how this spending will continue to increase as the pandemic rages on. Will our priorities shift, or will there be constant stimulus boosts?

These stimulus packages are very relevant in my community. I have some family members that even received aid when they had no job. These money boosts are a great help to everyone.

raw_comment:
1. I notice that the majority of stimulus bills were going to individuals and families, even more so than to businesses. Within this sector, stimulus checks made up a majority, with around $817 billion worth of checks. Also, I notice that the "other" category entails the U.S.P.S. loan of $10 billion, which is the smallest amount within this sector.

2. First, I wonder if the low amount of U.S.P.S. loans has something to do with their lack of funding from the government. In 2020, the lack of U.S.P.S. funding was a prominent issue, and the data could reflect this. Also, does this "businesses" sector include small businesses? I'd assume it does, but it just makes me think back to how hard it was (and still is) for them to keep their businesses afloat.

3. While I did not qualify for stimulus collection in 2020, my family was able to collect stimulus checks. I find it interesting to see how all of this money was distributed, especially since there were a lot of different uses for the money.

4. Stimulating Stimulus Data of 2020

raw_comment:
I noticed that the majority of the $5 trillion went to individuals and families ($1.8 trillion) and businesses ($1.7 trillion). The least amount of money went to other expenses ($288 billion). 

I wonder how they determine how much money is distributed between each category? Where does the unused money go? How long did it take for these stimulus bills to get passed? How did the release of $5 trillion affect the federal government?

This relates to me and my community because the federal money benefits everyone in the United States. The money that the government provided helped many businesses and individuals that were struggling during the pandemic. 

 This graph depicts where the $5 trillion stimulus funding went from the federal government. A catchy headline I came up with was “$5 Trillion to the United States Civilians”.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
These treemap graphs show how roughly $5 trillion of pandemic stimulus funding was allocated from March 2020 through Feb. Because of the Pandemic, the Fed released money into the world, about 5 trillion. While looking at the charts, the largest treemap graph was the Individuals and families graph for stimulus checks, next went to businesses for a paycheck protection program. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder what kind of impact the “extra” money flowing into the economy will have. Did the Fed and /or congress know what kind of inflation would occur when sending out the money? I wonder why the health care graph is second to the smallest, I would think it would be bigger due to Covid and medical bills. 
 
3. What impact does this have on you and your community? 
With more money being sent out by congress and the Fed, overtime our economy will see inflation (like now) and then they will have to control it by not making as much money to be released. Our economy will become more controlled to prevent any kind of depression. 
 
4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

raw_comment:
I notice that most of the money was put into individuals and families in terms of stimulus checks and unemployment benefits. Businesses also got a similar amount in terms of paycheck protection programs. I was surprised that more money didn't go to healthcare because of how much health care was used in the past couple of years with the spread of the Covid virus. Especially with an increase in regulations about vaccine and the initial implements of vaccines and the increase in Telehealth I assumed that would use up more money than shown on the graph. I also noticed that there was a small amount spend on election security which surprised me as well because there have been a lot of arguments about the recent elections and how secure they were. 

I wonder how it was determined what areas got a what amount or if it was based on what they needed? I also wonder how this all affects the inflation that is occurring in America. 

This relates to me because I have heard a lot on the news about the stimulus checks and how the government tries to help people after the spread of Covid 19 so it was interesting to see where all of the money went.

I noticed that each separate category contains five or more topics that have had high payment rates. Also, the bigger and larger the box is, the more money that was spend on that topic of interest. 

I wonder what bills and laws were passed that caused individuals and families to have the most money spent on the different topics beneath this category. My household got stimulus checks due to the pandemic. It did help us pay for certain things like heating in the winter so that was nice. Overall we only really used it for what we needed that we couldn't afford ourselves. Although the massive amounts of money sent was great for individual living the inflation made things go back to square 1.

raw_comment:
I notice that a lot of money is going to unemployment and stimulus checks which is probably raised due to Covid and families losing their job. I wonder if this will go down soon due to the World going back to "normal". I also think that since businesses are back and people need employees that the government should not have to give people stimulus checks since there is a need for employees and jobs out there. I also notice that Health care is far down the list from like businesses or state aid. It makes me wonder that since other countries have free health care I wonder if their spending looks a lot different from America's spending. Or I wonder what other countries value more to spend the most money on. Lastly I notice how every single box has a different amount of spending and I wonder if certain things are cheaper than others more like product based. Like is healthcare have less money because it takes less money to get vaccines then to hand out checks.

raw_comment:
I noticed that most of the stimulus funding was going into aids, both individually and locally. On an individual scale, a lot has been allocated to child care and elder's retirement benefits. Compared to that, spendings on infrascture pale.  As for healthcare, most was poured into vaccination. Quite considerable portion of the SB did go to business too.

I wondered what the aid could do to improve families financial situations, whether it could stimulates people to spend more and revitalize the economy? Or whether it might lead to  inflations and stagnations. I also curious about the  detailed implementation, wondering if it would be customized or an one-size-fit-all. Additionally I also wondered what it means for investments

I don't live in the US so I can't grasp a sense of its impacts. However I do wish to experience an overseas education here someday so following economics policies and grants/aids could really help me an insights into the situations. The fact that students loan was delayed is pertinent, but postpone could only go so far. Prior to this, I didn't know a delayed payments could cost such fortunes

I supposed "More stimulus bills approved? What does it say about the Biden administrations and its controversial impacts?"

raw_comment:
Thanks to all students who responded. Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received: “The Pandemic’s Damage Shown Through Stimulus Allocations” by Melissa; “Covid Stimulus: Who Got What?” by A of Portland, Oregon; “Stimulus Money: What America Prioritizes” by Natasha of Horizon High School in Winter Garden, Florida; “How is the Government Helping During the Pandemic?” by Annie, Mitchell, and Matt of Minnesota; and “Where the Stimulus Money Went: It's Here, There, and Everywhere!” by Abby, “Government Intervention and Economic Assistance During the Covid Pandemic” by Paige, “$5 Trillion vs. Covid-19” by Miriam, "US Congress Unleashed the Largest Stimulus Bill in Recorded History in 2020 - See Where the $5 Trillion Spent Went." by Jonah; “Once Upon a Stimmy,” by Alex; and “Staying Afloat, a Breakdown of $5 Trillion Distributed for COVID Support,” by Kaitlyn, all 6 of Oakland, California. 

You can continue to post responses.  Please check back by Friday, April 15 to see the Reveal with the free link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graphs, and a few Stat Nuggets.

raw_comment:
1. Families received $1.8 trillion dollars and that seems like a lot, but when you compare it to businesses it is only $0.1 trillion more. With government pricing, this is not that big of a difference. I feel that they most likely bumped the family money up just enough to present it as if they truly care for the American family rather than lending businesses to succeed. 
2. If we are trying to stop this pandemic, then why is Health Care only receiving $482 billion. It seems as if the government has put saving millions of lives on the back burner. I also wonder how much money from stimulus checks was wasted on wants rather than needs. I am sure some individuals truly needed the money and spent it wisely, but there had to be plenty of others who practically wasted it on things they normally could not afford and did not need.
3. As having a farm, affected me and my community. The government did provide us with a small amount of money, but it did not match the market. Beef prices skyrocketed in the grocery stores, yet it never really affected the selling price of beef for small farm owners at the stockyards. Everything else involving farming has increased, but the cattle themselves. This presents an opportunity for small farmers to fail.
4. Trying to Stop a Pandemic? Give Your Health Care Less Than Half a Billion Dollars

raw_comment:
In the Graph you can see how the congress' $5 trillion stimulus bills as a response to COVID were distributed into the US economy. You can see how individuals & families ($1.8 trillion) and businesses  ($1.7 trillion) were provided the most amount of financial aid. This funding was provided to help individuals who are either unemployed, potentially due to the pandemic, or have an insufficient stay afloat during this time of economic instability through stimulus checks and unemployment benefits which make up a large portion of the funding for individuals and families. 

I wonder how funding is typically distributed and whether or not individuals and families are usually such a large portion of annual government budgeting and if it isn't whether that is something we should change. There are high poverty rates throughout the US and specifically in large cities like Oakland so it is important that when constructing budgets and stimulus bills these issues should be addressed.

raw_comment:
Headline: Staying Afloat, a breakdown of $5 trillion distributed for COVID support

I noticed that majority(around half of the money distributed) went to helping individuals and families and businesses. COVID hit individuals who live paycheck to pay check and small businesses that barely break even really hard. Quarantine had people staying at home as much as they could so people who couldn't make enough money to stay open and who didn't have enough savings were forced to close. The money went to help they hold out until people went outside again and helped people who live almost paycheck to paycheck pay for rent or bills when they lost their jobs or had hours cut. I wonder how much the economy was actually stimulated with the money distributed. In my community, there are quite a few small businesses who had to close their doors since they couldn't make enough to keep the physical stores, I hope that the stimulus money helped a lot more stay open. The graph is a breakdown and physical representation of where the $5 trillion in stimulus money went to and tells us what COVID hit the hardest.

raw_comment:
Annie, Mitchell, and Matt 


Our catchy headline is “How is the government helping during the pandemic?” One thing that we noticed is that most of the money went to individuals, families, and businesses. We think this is most likely because families and businesses were impacted the most by covid. We thought most of the spending would go to businesses and healthcare. We are wondering if this is normal for individuals, families, and businesses to receive the most money or is this the cause of the pandemic.  This applies to us because it shows how covid is greatly affecting our community. We also all know of someone who has received a stimulus check or unemployment benefits.

raw_comment:
Noticed: it looks like this is a graph that is showing the breakdown of where the money from the stimulus bills issued during the pandemic went. There are 5 different groups in the graph, in order from largest to smallest based on the amount of money issued by the stimulus bills. The individuals and families & businesses groups had the most money issued by a pretty significant margin.
Wonder: how it was decided where the money went? Why so much of it went to individuals and families vs businesses or healthcare (especially during a pandemic)? How much government money goes towards these different groups of people or programs during a regular year? Would less people have died if more money had been spent on healthcare?

Headline: Who really gets the money?

We noticed that most of the money was allocated towards individuals and families, specifically through stimulus checks. Often times when we think of government funding we think it would go primarily to businesses, or health care facilities especially because of how overwhelming the pandemic was for these facilities. We wonder why so much of the money went to individuals and families and if this was just a result of COVID or if it was a normal occurrence. This plays a big impact on seeing how we as a society are supported and where the money we put into the government actually goes.

raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graphs show the federal funds that went to households, businesses large and small, local governments, schools and other institutions around the country for the two years from March 2020 to February 28, 2022.  The purpose of the $5 trillion stimulus infusion was to help Americans financially from the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic.   

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?”, “What do you wonder?"  and “How will this affect you and your community?”  Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in these graphs. 

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the article that included these graphs and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

Note that you can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).
View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, April 15 with moderation on Wednesday, April 20.  The topic – U.S. population dynamics.

1. I noticed that most of the stimulus check was allocated to unemployment benefits and paycheck (protection) programs of all sorts, with all of these pertaining to the concept of paid leaves (regardless of whether or not people actually caught the virus). 

2. I wonder why so much less money was spent on health care, despite the very purpose of this stimulus check being to help people out during the Pandemic? 

3. On April 2nd, 2022, my state sent $500 checks to 500K low-income workers. 

4. "The Dispersion of Our Governmental Money From the River's Bank"

raw_comment:
1. The sheer amount of money that is being spent. It's inconceivable honestly. A majority of the money was distributed to those unable to work due to covid allowing citizens to still be able to provide for themselves. 
2. Since there is an "other" section in almost all the sections and each of these brackets houses more than 10 billion dollars each, I wonder what is put into these sections. I also wonder why the health care section is proportional very small in the grand scheme of things.
3. I know so many people who depended on stimulus checks since the virus made it either unsafe or impossible to complete their work to provide for themselves. But then there is the other side to it where health care is, for many people, inaccessible due to its expense. 
4. What is the government really spending its money on?

raw_comment:
1 - Health care is actually a pretty large portion of the budget, compared to other areas, however, considering this is in response to the pandemic, I would actually expect it to be even more. 
2 - The main things which I wonder are the impacts this will have on the federal budgets of fiscal year 2021 and onward. This may be only part of the changes we are seeing towards economic policy due to the pandemic.
3 - The most noticeable impacts are 1) the economic changes due to the pandemic itself and 2) the direct (but rather small on an individual level) stream of money coming in the form of stimulus checks. Other impacts, such as unemployment and inflation, can be attributed to some mix of both the pandemic itself, and the government's response to the pandemic. An interesting impact which I see is that many who have not lost their jobs have started investing in the stock market due to the stimulus checks. Due to us being in uncertain times, a lot of that has gone into large companies with relatively "safe" stocks. In my opinion, this leads to very low amounts of economic "stimulation", for it's cost in inflation.
4 - "Pandemic Response at a Glance."

What's going on in this graph?

raw_comment:
1. Regarding the graph I noticed that it is firstly divided into 5 primary categories, being businesses, individuals and families, state and local aid, and health care, and within those categories there are more specific supported areas. I was surprised to see how much aid was given to the individual rather than larger aid systems such as businesses and health care. 

2. I wonder if it may have been better to supply more aid to organizations such as businesses and health care, however that aid would have to be put towards the individuals under those businesses. I believe that this may ensure that the aid being given would be used proactively rather than it possibly being spent on unnecessary things. 

3. The COVID-19 pandemic greatly affected a lot of the small businesses in my community alongside my smaller school. Many of the family owned restaurants in my village had to close down for over a year or sell out their business to a larger branch. Also Personally COVID-19 halted many of my personal progression. This pandemic didn't allow me to as explore extra circulars and explore my future options after high school with the shelter in place mandate, which effected me greatly.

4. This graph summarizes how the $5 trillion the U.S govt aided was distributed to the people, businesses, state and local aid, health care, etc. in which I personally believe a good headline would be: What the U.S government Decided to do with 5 Trillion Dollars in Aid Since the COVID-19 Outbreak.

raw_comment:
I notice that 36% of the stimulus was given to individuals and families with a quantity of $1.8 Trillion. I also notice that this stimulus was given for covid-19 yet they gave more money to individuals rather than health care by a large amount without counting the stimulus given to businesses. Airlines were given  $80 bil. since airplanes were thought to be extremely bad because of covid and tickets were extremely low. Probably funding for the importation of goods instead of commercial use.

I wonder how big of an impact would the money not include that was approved by administrative or Federal Reserve action would affect this graph. How much money are we leaving out Billions, Trillion, or just millions? 

This has an impact on my community and the economic aspect, especially on gas and goods. The inflation in our community is being felt by everyone, gas has reached a peak and stayed there for a relatively long time. The combination of inflation and the war stopping certain goods from arriving in America is hurting our community.

My headline would be: How was the stimulus distributed and what were America's priorities?

raw_comment:
There is a ton of money flowing through to these programs and grants but still many of these programs constantly hurt for money. Also some of the money is being allocated in unequal and almost foolish ways. 41 billion dollars were given to farmers and 678 billion dollars were to unemployment. We are currently in an unemployment crisis and the government continues to pour into it. 
 
Why is so much money being wasted in grants and programs in order to “fix” the economy. Wouldn’t it be better to run things like it was before covid and let everything straighten itself out. Even if some businesses fail and go bankrupt, isn't it better to let them fail and have new businesses start up to eventually take the baton so to speak instead of raising inflation and bailing out businesses just to make sure they stay powerful. 

I live in a community where all these different grants and programs are not only needed but necessary. I know personally how much the trickle down effect really affects us and I can say there hasn’t been much of a difference. I’m not saying that everyone should be driving Mercedes Benz and living in mansions but over 5 trillion dollars has been dispersed between 329.5 million Americans and we are still living paycheck to paycheck. 
 
The graph is showing how all the money printed during covid was allocated to different grants, loans, programs, funds etc. “How were 5 trillion tax dollars allocated during the pandemic”

raw_comment:
I notice...
I notice that most of the money went to individuals and families. The distribution of the stimulus checks shows that the government put more importance on families, individuals, businesses, and state and local aid rather than on health care.

I wonder...
I wonder why the government didn't put more importance on health care since it includes vaccine development which would've ended the pandemic sooner rather than later.

What impact do you think this has on you and your community?
The GIANT sum of 5 trillion dollars that the government gave out must have been some kind of deficit spending. As much as it is nice to have an increase in your bank account deficit spending creates an increase in inflation and taxes. As a country, we need to find a way to decrease inflation and deficit spending so that the people can keep more of their money rather than pay taxes. If we don't solve the problem and instead try to hide it, the prices for life's necessities will continue to go up affecting every family and community in America.

Headline
Nothing Comes Free-- Not Even Stimulus Checks.

raw_comment:
In the graph, I notice that most of the stimulus money went towards individuals and families, closely followed by businesses. They gave the least amount of money to health care and the other category.  
I wonder what determined where the government decided to give the money, and where are they getting 5 trillion dollars from if we are so in debt? 
I think that this affected a lot of people in my community because it got a lot of people used to pay without working and I think that this lowered our community's work ethic. A lot of places are now urgently hiring, but not enough people are going back to work. This also shows us where our taxes are going and what we are supporting with our money. Our money is going towards others' stimulus checks and helping to support businesses. 

Are you working so others don't have to?!?!

I notice that there are different sized boxes for the amount of money spent, the bigger the box, the higher the money, and there are different colors for each category, like Individuals and Families, Businesses, State and Local Aid, Health Care, etc. 

I wonder where they got the data from and where the money came from. I also wonder why they are still spending this crazy amount of money even though we are in extreme debt. 

I think this impacts our community because we are getting to the age where we are going to have to start paying our own taxes soon enough and we should know where our tax money is going and why taxes have been increasing.

raw_comment:
Compared to other categories, American Healthcare is grossly underfunded. We are falling well short of making healthcare accessible to all. If other countries with a lot fewer resources than us can do it, we can too.

How does this compare to government spending before the Covid 19 pandemic? What areas are getting more funding and what areas are getting less? How much does this amount of spending range from year to year typically?

This relates to me and my community because this spending is (hopefully) intended to benefit the lives of Americans. This money is also being spent by a government that only works if it is respected by its country's citizens (our community) so we must always be analyzing the actions of this government we chose to put in power.

"Investigating America's Investments"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that within the graph the majority of that $5 trillion in federal money went directly towards individuals and families and businesses. Then when looking further I noticed that the specific category in which the most money went to, was the paycheck protection program with stimulus checks receiving about 18 billion less.

What do you wonder?
I wonder how it is that Congress came to decide how to split the money and what determined each category's importance. I also wonder about the impact that giving greater amounts of money to certain causes over others.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because after the pandemic a great amount of my community faced the unfortunate results of covid going into unemployment or fighting the illness itself along with many other factors. The graph provides us with information as to where exactly the money went to and brings awareness to the turnout of that money.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?  After analyzing the graph, I saw the two highest aspects of this graph were “businesses” and “individuals and families.”  The Paycheck protection program and stimulus checks are the biggest contributors in these sections.  Health care was surprising low compared to these two categories, even though the things inside provide huge contributions to our country (ie. vaccines and supplies).  
 
 
 
 
What do you wonder?  Why is health care, an important and necessary thing, insignificant compared to businesses and “individuals and families.”
 
 
 
 
How does this relate to you and your community?  Things like unemployment saw a dramatic increase around the time of the pandemic.  This could explain the large amount of contributions made to things such as this.  The economy was also failing at this time due to a lot of businesses closing. This would explain the large amount of money put towards businesses and other financial aids around this time.  
 
 
 
 
What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
“The Money Frenzy” can be a good headline to describe these uprisings.  It describes the existential amount of money that was needed to keep our country from collapsing.

raw_comment: I notice that in each category, a large amount of the $5 trillion of stimulus money was going to mostly one subcategory. For example, in the individuals and families category, most of the $1.8 trillion went to stimulus checks and unemployment benefits. These were important to provide people with because lots of people lost their jobs because companies were struggling to stay open during the pandemic. People needed money to support themselves. Another example would be how the $1.7 trillion allocated to businesses went to paycheck protections and economic injury disasters. This makes sense, because lots of companies were struggling to stay open and pay their employees. When they received stimulus payments, they could keep their employees and stay open. I wonder why the health care section did not get more funding. Although $482 billion is quite a lot, health care is very important during a pandemic and putting more funding into it would allow for processes, like developing vaccines, to be faster and more effective. With more money, they can spend on more materials. This relates to me and my community because a lot of people were impacted by the pandemic. Lots of people lost their jobs, their companies, and loved ones. All of those things are expensive and providing the American people with stimulus money was very helpful to help get the country back on their feet. A catchy headline for this graph would be “The Pandemic’s Damage Shown Through Stimulus Allocations.”

Majority of these stimulus checks were given to families and businesses. Though a large portion was given to businesses and aid, healthcare was one of the lowest paid sections. During the pandemic, health was a priority, so it is odd that businesses were given more money than healthcare.

Why was healthcare neglected compared to other sections? 
How many small businesses are there that suffered through the pandemic?
Where did the money come from? (taxes?)

- I wonder why federal funding prioritizes business and individuals over health care and education because these directly impact everyone as well as our society and future. I also wonder when stimulus checks will stop being sent out.

With the high amount of money going towards unemployment benefits, it encourages the lazy and unemployed to stay lazy.
- In this graph, we are seeing where the government is placing money they are printing as well as tax-payer dollars. A headline that captures the graph’s main idea would be “Government Money? Print and Spend”

raw_comment:
I notice that there is a lot of money going into all of these programs, but I did not know about a lot of them. I also notice that the money that went into “Individuals and Families” and “Businesses” is the same, yet small businesses around the country are struggling.


 
I wonder where our country’s priorities are and where they intend to focus on growth. Why are they focussing on giving everyone money, but then not focussing on helping people make their own money?

 
My dad owns a small business and when money was given to help support small businesses, he was not given anything. This most likely happened to other businesses around my area and is causing a downward spiral in my community.

A catchy headline could be “The Money Mystery”

raw_comment:
I notice that there is a lot of money going into all of these programs. Even the programs that seem like they weren't given a lot of money were still given billions of dollars. That is an unfathomable amount of money and they make it seem like it's this tiny amount.

raw_comment: The first thing that I noticed was paid a small amount (in comparison to the other sectors listed). This is interesting to me because I expected there to be a much higher focus on that sector, considering it is a global pandemic and I feel it should be a high priority to focus on eliminating the spread of the virus. While education, businesses, and individual families are important, I would have expected a more even spread between the four sectors. This relates to me and my community because I know people who had their business affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, and as well as that I know the effects that it had on people's education. Businesses had difficulty staying afloat during this time period, and as a result a lot ended up going out of business due to the extended lockdown. In addition, I know personally that I felt worse doing virtual learning as opposed learning in person. However, if more money was given to the healthcare sector, they could have avoided this completely by cutting off the pandemic when it started, and this could have been achieved by putting more time, effort, and financial aid into healthcare. If I had to make a headline for these graphs, I would probably name it "5 trillion dollars, where did it go?"

What do you notice:

Stimulus Checks was the biggest in Individuals and families, Paycheck Protection Program was the biggest in Businesses, 
American Rescue Plan direct aid was the biggest in state and local aid,
Grants to health providers was the biggest in Health Care,

Our local schools, our local economy, and our families

Bils and Trils,
*money eyes emoji*
Balling on a budget
Spending in Covid

I wonder how effective some of the spending was such as allocating funds toward housing projects and medicaid coverage.
